title: Operational Psychological Safety and Debrief Protocols
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document defines the operational psychological safety (ops-psych) principles and a standardized debrief protocol for incidents, game days, and on-call rotations. The goal is to protect responder wellbeing, improve learning throughput from incidents, and reduce blame-based behaviors that slow down remediation. This is intended to supplement existing incident triage and postmortem processes and applies to all responder roles (first-responder, bridge operator, service steward, and on-call engineers).

Scope:
- Applies to incidents, near-misses, game days, and sustained SLO restoration efforts.
- Covers pre-incident preparation, in-incident communication hygiene, immediate debrief (T+0–24h), and in-depth postmortem synthesis.

Principles (short):
1) People over logs: protect human responders before preserving artifacts.
2) Curious, not accusatory: ask what, how, and why — avoid who-first language.
3) Timely, lightweight learning: capture actionable fixes within 24–48 hours.
4) Iterative improvement: validate fixes via follow-up game days or synthetic checks.

Roles & Ownership:
- Incident Lead (IL): coordinates response and ensures an immediate debrief is scheduled.
- Bridge Operator: runs incident bridge, documents decisions and action owners.
- Steward / Service Owner: owns follow-up remediation and postmortem delivery.
- People-Ops Liaison: supports psychological-safety interventions for high-impact incidents and organizes peer support.

Before an Incident (preparation):
- Mandatory: each responder completes the Ops-Psych micro-course (20 min) and acknowledges the debrief playbook.
- Runbooks must include an explicit ‘people check’ step (owner contact, rotation backup).
- Rotation managers maintain a visible on-call load index per engineer (weekly snapshot). Target max weekly load index = 1.0 (see below).

During an Incident (communication hygiene):
- Use neutral language templates in bridge chat (examples below).
- Pause non-essential escalations during high-cognitive-load phases.
- Assign a single communications lead for external messages.

Immediate Debrief (T+0 to T+24h) — Template and Steps:
1. Schedule: IL schedules 30–45 minute debrief within 6 hours of mitigation or bridge close.
2. Attendees: responders on-shift, bridge operator, service owner, one People-Ops or SRE mentor. Keep attendance voluntary beyond core responders.
3. Agenda (structured):
   - 00–05m: Safety check-in (How is everyone? Any immediate support needed?)
   - 05–10m: Brief factual timeline (no finger-pointing)
   - 10–25m: What surprised us? What worked?
   - 25–35m: Immediate action owners & near-term mitigations (within 72h)
   - 35–45m: Communication plan for customers and leadership, and schedule for postmortem
4. Outputs (must be captured in incident ticket):
   - One-sentence incident summary
   - 3 short observations (factual)
   - 2 proposed actions with owners and target dates
   - People check (who needs follow-up support)

Postmortem Quality Gate (T+24–72h):
- Draft postmortem should be created within 72 hours and include the Immediate Debrief outputs.
- Postmortems must pass the following quality checklist before publication:
  * Clear timeline with source links to traces/alerts (yes/no)
  * Action owners assigned with due dates (yes/no)
  * Root cause analysis focused on systems and processes (not individuals) (yes/no)
  * Proposed verification plan for fixes (smoke tests/game-day) (yes/no)
  * Short executive summary (≤3 sentences) (yes/no)

Runbook Validation Checklist:
- Each runbook entry must include: triggers, quick mitigations (2–3 bullets), escalations, owner contact, and a ‘people-safe’ note (how to pause and request backup).
- Quarterly: sample each high-severity runbook via one simulated run by a cross-team pair.
- Validation Result Table (example):
| Runbook | Last Tested | Tester | Pass/Fail | Notes |
| Serving-GPU-OOM | 2026-05-10 | infra-sim | Pass | Added KV-cache eviction step |

Game Day Debrief Agenda (60–90m):
- Pre-game warmup (15m): technical goals and safety norms
- Simulation window (varies, recorded)
- After-action review (50m): start with feelings check, then timeline, then improvements
- Decide owner and date for follow-up verification

Customer Status and Leadership Communication Templates (examples):
- Short customer status (for live incidents, 2–3 lines):
  "We are investigating increased latency for Redwood text-generation in us-west-2. Our engineers have mitigated the immediate impact and are working on a full restoration. We will provide a next update within 60 minutes. If you need priority support, reply to this message or contact your CSM."

- Leadership incident brief (email/exec summary):
  Subject: [INC] us-west-2 latency — mitigated, investigation ongoing
  Body: 1) What happened (1 line) 2) Impact (tokens/sec, % customers affected) 3) Current status (mitigated/partially degraded) 4) Next steps (owner + ETA)

Neutral Language Examples for Bridge/Chat:
- Instead of: "Who broke the KV cache?" use: "What sequence of events led to the KV cache eviction?"
- Instead of: "You missed the alert" use: "Which alert thresholds did we see and how did they behave?"

Escalation and People-Support Paths:
- For high-stress incidents (severity ≥ 1 hour outage impacting >10% customers) People-Ops will offer a short 1:1 check-in with each on-call participant within 48 hours.
- For traumatic incidents (data loss or customer breach) the company will fund a confidential external counseling session on request.

Action Tracking and Follow-up:
- Use the incident tracker (Jira ticket pattern: INC-YYYY-NNNN). All actions must be entered as subtasks with due dates.
- SRE steward reviews open actions weekly; overdue items escalate to the service owner and responsibility forum.

Measurement and Success Criteria:
- Target: 90% of Immediate Debriefs completed within 24 hours for severity P1/P2 incidents.
- Target: 100% of postmortem quality gates passed for Sev1s within 30 days.
- People metric: reduce oncall burnout index (anonymous pulse) by 20% year-over-year via rotation adjustments and psych-safety interventions.

Appendix A — Short checklists (copyable):
Immediate Debrief Checklist:
- [ ] Schedule 30–45m session within 6 hours
- [ ] Include People-Ops or SRE mentor
- [ ] Capture outputs (1-line summary, 3 observations, 2 actions with owners)

Postmortem Quality Gate Checklist:
- [ ] Timeline with links
- [ ] Actions with owners and dates
- [ ] Root cause analysis (systems/processes)
- [ ] Verification plan
- [ ] Exec summary

Customer Status Template (longer for public status page):
- Title: Degraded performance for Redwood text generation — us-west-2
- Status: Investigating / Identified / Partial restoration / Restored
- Impact: Users may experience 2–10x latency on text-generation routes; embeddings unaffected
- Next update: Timestamp + ETA
- Workaround: Retry with model-redwood-lite or fall back to regional routing (eu-central-1)

Guidance for Rotation Managers (operational):
- Rebalance rotation if a single engineer’s 4-week load index > 1.2.
- Encourage scheduled recovery days after two P1 incidents in a 30-day window.
- Maintain a confidential incident-impact log for each on-call participant (for People-Ops review only).
